audit.whatIsWrong: Pantheon is repeatedly given an attack-blocking passive: 'his passive block eats your first retaliatory auto' (whys[0]), 'his empowered auto passive blocks your next basic attack' (early), 'his passive block still eats one auto per empowered window' (late), 'his passive block is wasted on your slow autos' (spikes[3]), 'his passive block is meaningless' (whys[6]).
audit.why: Pantheon's passive is Mortal Will: every few spells or attacks his next spell is empowered. It blocks nothing. The blocking is Aegis Assault, his E — and that is a completely different thing to play around, because it is a channel with a 22-second cooldown rather than a free recurring effect. Five strings teach the player to fear an ability that is not in the kit.
audit.corrected: Mortal Will empowers his next spell every few casts. The damage block is Aegis Assault (E), and it is not free.
sources: champ-data/_kits/pantheon.json P Mortal Will, E Aegis Assault

audit.whatIsWrong: Aegis Assault is never named in either layer, despite being the ability that decides whether Tahm Kench's commit lands.
audit.why: Three things about it matter and none are stated. It is a channel, so any hard crowd control cancels it — the 3-stack Tongue Lash stun ends it outright, as does an Abyssal Dive knockup. It makes him invulnerable to damage FROM THE FRONT, so walking behind him beats it rather than waiting it out. And at 22/21/20/19/18s it is the longest non-ultimate cooldown he has, which makes it the best thing in the matchup to bait. The missing-interactions file flags this pairing from both directions.
audit.corrected: Your 3-stack stun cancels Aegis Assault. It only shields the front. It is 22s at rank 1 — bait it and the window is enormous.
sources: champ-data/_kits/pantheon.json E Aegis Assault flags channel/untargetable/shield

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Pantheon 6 of 7 stages in a matchup Tahm Kench wins 56.58%. It also contradicts the file's own prose — spikes[2] calls first item 'the lane turn' while win[5] still reads Pantheon.
audit.why: Two of the six Pantheon stages do not survive checking. Level 1 was justified by a passive block that does not exist, and first item is described everywhere else as the point the lane flips.
audit.corrected: win[0] Pantheon -> Skill (the stated reason for his level-1 edge was a fabricated passive); win[5] Pantheon -> Skill (matches spikes[2]). Final shape Pantheon 4 / Skill 2 / Tahm Kench 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers say to trade around Shield Vault's cooldown; neither gives it, or any other number.
audit.why: Grand Starfall in particular is 180s at rank 1 — the longest cooldown either champion has. A spent Starfall is three minutes of guaranteed map safety, and nothing tells the player that.
audit.corrected: Shield Vault 13/12/11/10/9s at 600. Aegis Assault 22/21/20/19/18s. Comet Spear 11/10.25/9.5/8.75/8s. Grand Starfall 180/165/150s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shield Vault is called a 'point-click W stun' with no mention that it resets his auto-attack.
audit.why: The dash carries an auto reset, which is why the burst arrives faster than the ability animations suggest. The wind-up on the landing, not the cast, is the timing cue for Thick Skin's shield.
audit.corrected: Shield Vault resets his auto — the landing is the cue, not the cast.
sources: champ-data/_kits/pantheon.json W Shield Vault flags autoReset

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1], content.mid and content.late all give Tahm Kench 'Abyssal Voyage' as a counter-roam and objective tool.
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the pre-rework ultimate and is not in the current kit. Level 6 gives Devour, which is not a map-tempo answer to Grand Starfall at all — the honest answer is that a spent Starfall is a 180-second window, not that you can match his roam.
audit.corrected: Level 6 gives Devour. Against Grand Starfall you play the 180s cooldown, not a roam race.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] and whys[6] treat 'stun-Devour' and 'W stun into Devour' as single combos.
audit.why: Tongue Lash on a three-stack target stuns and consumes the stacks; devouring an enemy champion requires three stacks. Against a burst champion where the stack window is short, the choice matters more than usual — the stun cancels Aegis Assault, the Devour removes him.
audit.corrected: Three stacks buys the stun or the Devour.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's Common Mistakes entry lists 'Sit low for his W execute'.
audit.why: Shield Vault is a dash that damages and stuns. Nothing in Pantheon's kit is flagged as an execute. The advice points at a threat that does not exist while the real one — spending three stacks into a live Aegis Assault instead of cancelling it — goes unmentioned.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the real mistakes: waiting on a passive block he does not have, and burning the stack cycle into Aegis Assault rather than cancelling it.

audit.why: whys[0] claims Comet Spear outranges Tongue Lash at level 1. I did not change that claim. The kit lists Comet Spear at 575 and describes two cast modes — 'either thrusts his spear or throws his spear' — so the single range figure plainly does not cover the thrown form, and I cannot establish the throw range from the files on disk. Left the claim alone rather than asserting a number in either direction.

notes: The 'passive block' fiction is the headline here: five separate strings tell the player Pantheon's passive blocks his autos. It does not — Mortal Will empowers his next spell, and the block is Aegis Assault (E). This one is worth a champion-wide grep, because it looks like pre-rework Pantheon knowledge (Aegis Protection) that survived into the current text, the same way 'Abyssal Voyage' did on Tahm Kench's side. The flip side is that Aegis Assault was never named anywhere in this matchup despite being the highest-value interaction in it: 22s cooldown, frontal-only invulnerability, and a channel that any hard CC — including the 3-stack Tongue Lash stun — cancels outright. Both directions of the missing-interactions file flag this pairing and neither was acted on. I deliberately did NOT touch whys[0]'s claim that Comet Spear outranges Tongue Lash: the kit lists Q at 575 with a description covering both a thrust and a throw, so the single figure cannot settle it and I had nothing verified to replace it with. Chart change is Medium confidence — I moved two of six Pantheon stages to Skill on the strength of the file's own contradicting prose, not on an independent read of the matchup. No WKM_LINES errors observed.
